title: Sections of a sheaf on a basis are the families of germs satisfying (*)
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $\mathcal B$ a set of open subsets of $X$ which is a basis of the topology and satisfies $U\cap V\in\mathcal B$ for $U,V\in\mathcal B$. Let $F$ be a presheaf of abelian groups on $\mathcal B$ (groups $F(U)$, $U\in\mathcal B$, restriction homomorphisms $r_{U,V}$, $s|_V=r_{U,V}(s)$, with $r_{U,U}=\mathrm{id}$ and $r_{V,W}r_{U,V}=r_{U,W}$) such that for every $U\in\mathcal B$, every family $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ of members of $\mathcal B$ with $\bigcup_iU_i=U$ ($I$ arbitrary, possibly empty) and every family $s_i\in F(U_i)$ with $s_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=s_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}$ for all $i,j$ there is exactly one $s\in F(U)$ with $s|_{U_i}=s_i$ for all $i$. For $x\in X$ let $F_x$ be the stalk of $F$ at $x$ with germ maps $\sigma\mapsto\sigma_x$ [def-weil-pbc-basis-presheaf-stalk]. Then for every $U\in\mathcal B$ the map $\gamma_U:F(U)\to\prod_{x\in U}F_x$, $s\mapsto(s_x)_{x\in U}$, is injective, and its image is the set of families $(t_x)_{x\in U}$ with property (*): for every $x\in U$ there are $V\in\mathcal B$ with $x\in V\subseteq U$ and $\sigma\in F(V)$ with $t_y=\sigma_y$ for all $y\in V$.

source.place: Section 009H, Lemma 009M (label lemma-condition-star-sections) and its proof (for a sheaf of sets on B, Definition 009J; by Lemma 009L (label lemma-cofinal-systems-coverings-standard-case) with B closed under intersections the hypothesis here is that sheaf condition); for values in abelian groups, the remark before Lemma 009Q that 009K, 009L, 009M hold without change for the underlying presheaf of sets

proof.text: *Injectivity of $\gamma_W$ for every $W\in\mathcal B$.* Let $W\in\mathcal B$ and $s,s'\in F(W)$ with $s_x=s'_x$ in $F_x$ for every $x\in W$. Fix $x\in W$. By the description of equality in the directed colimit $F_x=\operatorname{colim}_{V\in\mathcal B_x}F(V)$ [def-weil-pbc-basis-presheaf-stalk] (two elements $\sigma\in F(V)$, $\sigma'\in F(V')$, $V,V'\in\mathcal B_x$, have the same germ at $x$ if and only if there is $V''\in\mathcal B_x$ with $V''\subseteq V\cap V'$ and $r_{V,V''}\sigma=r_{V',V''}\sigma'$), applied with $V=V'=W$, there is $V_x\in\mathcal B$ with $x\in V_x\subseteq W$ and $s|_{V_x}=s'|_{V_x}$. Choose such a $V_x$ for every $x\in W$. Then $(V_x)_{x\in W}$ is a family of members of $\mathcal B$ with $\bigcup_{x\in W}V_x=W$ (each $x\in W$ lies in $V_x\subseteq W$; for $W=\emptyset$ it is the empty family, allowed in the hypothesis). The family $s_x^\ast=s|_{V_x}\in F(V_x)$ is compatible: $s|_{V_x}|_{V_x\cap V_y}=s|_{V_x\cap V_y}=s|_{V_y}|_{V_x\cap V_y}$ by $r_{V,W'}r_{U,V}=r_{U,W'}$ (all intersections lie in $\mathcal B$). Both $s$ and $s'$ restrict to it, since $s'|_{V_x}=s|_{V_x}$. By the uniqueness half of the gluing hypothesis for the $\mathcal B$-covering $(V_x)_{x\in W}$ of $W$, $s=s'$. Hence $\gamma_W$ is injective; for $W=U$ this is the first claim.

source.place: Section 009H, proof of Lemma 009M (label lemma-condition-star-sections), first sentence: 'injective by the uniqueness in the sheaf condition of Definition 009J'; the equality of germs in the directed colimit F_x after Definition 009I (label definition-presheaf-basis) written out

proof.text: *The image satisfies (*).* Let $s\in F(U)$ and $t=\gamma_U(s)$, i.e. $t_y=s_y$ for $y\in U$. For $x\in U$ take $V=U\in\mathcal B$ (so $x\in V\subseteq U$) and $\sigma=s\in F(V)$; then $t_y=\sigma_y$ for all $y\in V$. So $\gamma_U(F(U))$ is contained in the set of families with (*).

source.place: Section 009H, Lemma 009M (label lemma-condition-star-sections), the inclusion of the image in the families with (*), not written in Stacks

proof.text: *Every family with (*) is in the image.* Let $t=(t_x)_{x\in U}\in\prod_{x\in U}F_x$ satisfy (*). For each $x\in U$ choose $V_x\in\mathcal B$ with $x\in V_x\subseteq U$ and $\sigma_x\in F(V_x)$ with $t_y=(\sigma_x)_y$ for all $y\in V_x$. Then $(V_x)_{x\in U}$ is a $\mathcal B$-covering of $U$ ($x\in V_x\subseteq U$; for $U=\emptyset$ the empty family). Compatibility: let $x,x'\in U$ and $W=V_x\cap V_{x'}$, which lies in $\mathcal B$ by the hypothesis on $\mathcal B$. For $z\in W$, by the compatibility of germs with restriction [def-weil-pbc-basis-presheaf-stalk], $(\sigma_x|_W)_z=(\sigma_x)_z=t_z=(\sigma_{x'})_z=(\sigma_{x'}|_W)_z$. So $\sigma_x|_W,\sigma_{x'}|_W\in F(W)$ have the same germ at every point of $W$, and by step 1 applied to $W\in\mathcal B$ (this is where the uniqueness half of the hypothesis enters, for the covering of $V_x\cap V_{x'}$ found there) $\sigma_x|_W=\sigma_{x'}|_W$. By the existence half of the gluing hypothesis for the covering $(V_x)_{x\in U}$ there is $s\in F(U)$ with $s|_{V_x}=\sigma_x$ for every $x\in U$. For $y\in U$, $y\in V_y$ and $s_y=(s|_{V_y})_y=(\sigma_y)_y=t_y$ [def-weil-pbc-basis-presheaf-stalk]. Hence $\gamma_U(s)=t$. Together with steps 1 and 2: $\gamma_U$ is injective with image exactly the families satisfying (*).
